hints: uncaught exception traceback showing in bract error output
multi-line error message
how should errors be formatted in bract
ad hoc print or raise for an error
req-0138.statement: Every error Bract reports (lex, parse, or runtime) is a single line on stderr in the exact form `line N: <message>` (1-indexed line), sourced from one shared error-formatting path — no stack traces, exception class names, ANSI color, or secondary lines. Every failure path must be caught and re-rendered through this format before reaching the user.

hints: deep recursion stack overflow in bract program
should I just raise sys.setrecursionlimit
RecursionError on deep call chain
iterative vs recursive tree-walking interpreter
how to support deep recursion without blowing the python stack
req-0a08.statement: The Bract evaluator must not use Python's own call stack for recursive evaluation; implement function calls and nested block execution with an explicit stack/work-list instead.

hints: bare x = expr not parsing
assignment without let or set keyword
redeclaring a let variable in the same scope
set on an undeclared name
how do closures mutate captured state in bract
req-1682.statement: (Q2) `let x = expr;` declares a new binding and errors (`line N: 'x' is already declared`) if `x` already exists in that exact scope; `set x = expr;` reassigns an existing binding found by walking the scope chain outward and errors (`line N: 'x' is not declared`) if none exists. There is no bare `x = expr;` form — it's a parse error.

hints: task prompt disagrees with the spec which one wins
DESIGN.md and task description conflict
spec vs task instructions contradiction
req-21d5.statement: Where DESIGN.md and a task description conflict, treat the conflict as a bug to flag, not license to guess.

hints: adding a new entry point script for bract fmt
where does CLI dispatch live
separate script for each CLI subcommand
req-2aa0.statement: (SC10) Every CLI entry point (`bract`, `bract run`, `bract fmt`) is dispatched from a single `bract/__main__.py` — there is no second top-level script.

hints: why is bract run printing extra output
does bract run echo expression results
difference between REPL and file execution output
unexpected output when running a bract file
req-2e63.statement: `bract run FILE` must not do the REPL's implicit result-printing — it should only emit output the program itself writes, plus the one-line error format on failure.

hints: should and/or short-circuit in bract
side effect not running in right operand of and
non-short-circuit boolean evaluation
does or stop evaluating after first true
req-31bd.statement: (Q7) `and`/`or` never short-circuit — both operands are always evaluated in left-to-right order regardless of the left operand's value, so side effects in the right operand always happen. Both operands must be Boolean.

hints: should numbers auto-convert to strings
implicit coercion between int and bool
why is there no float type in bract
req-3a6d.statement: There is no float type and no implicit type conversion anywhere in Bract — every operator's operand types are fixed and a mismatch is always a runtime type error, never a coercion.

hints: should we rename the bract project
is the name bract already taken
why isn't this project called sprout
req-3de8.statement: The project's working name 'Sprout' was rejected due to collisions with at least four existing languages (including a same-shaped Python tree-walking interpreter on PyPI); the chosen name 'Bract' was explicitly checked for collisions and found clear (nearest hits: an unrelated Clojure config framework and the unrelated Bracmat language).

hints: REPL crashing on a bad statement
should REPL exit after an error
bract repl error handling behavior
req-3f9e.statement: The REPL does not exit on a per-statement error — it reports the error the same way as any other error and continues reading the next statement.

hints: string concatenation with plus not working
+'' cannot be applied to strings error
how do I concatenate strings in bract
using + like Python or JS for strings
req-5f10.statement: (Q3) `~` concatenates two strings and only two strings; `+` is exclusively integer addition. Applying `+` to one or two strings is a type error (`line N: '+' cannot be applied to strings`), not string concatenation or coercion.

hints: a test is failing should I edit the test
fix the code or fix the test
test file modification not allowed when fixing failures
req-624b.statement: When tests are failing, fix the implementation — never modify the test files to make them pass.

hints: let inside while loop colliding across iterations
closures not capturing the right variable
does fn close over its defining scope in bract
counter closure pattern
req-7014.statement: A block's lexical scope is created fresh every time it's entered — each `while` iteration and each function call starts with an empty innermost scope, so a `let` inside a loop body declares anew each iteration rather than colliding with the previous one. `fn` values close over their defining environment as real closures (a returned inner `fn` still sees outer `let` bindings after the outer call returns).

hints: bract fmt changing code semantics
does fmt overwrite the source file in place
formatter reordering expressions
canonical formatter AST preservation
req-7c4f.statement: `bract fmt FILE` writes a canonically formatted version to stdout without modifying the source file, and only ever changes whitespace, indentation, and brace placement — it never reorders, re-associates, or drops AST nodes (expression grouping, operator precedence, and evaluation order are exactly preserved).

hints: what should the REPL prompt text be
Ctrl-D crashes the REPL
EOF handling in interactive mode
repl exit code on stdin close
uncaught EOFError in repl
req-7ff3.statement: The REPL prompt string must be exactly 'bract> ' (with one trailing space), and EOF on stdin (Ctrl-D) must end the session cleanly with exit code 0 — never raise an uncaught exception.

hints: using print() for debugging in evaluator.py
stray print statement in the lexer
global dict for variable bindings
test failures from shared state between runs
req-8843.statement: (SC4/SC8) No `print()` or stdout/stderr writes outside the CLI entry point, and no module-level mutable interpreter state (no global dict/list for bindings, call stack, or output) — lexer/parser/evaluator communicate only through return values and exceptions, with all interpreter state threaded explicitly through an Environment/Interpreter instance.

hints: adding s[0] indexing syntax to the parser
bracket indexing for strings
subscript operator not in the grammar
convenience syntax for string access
req-9328.statement: There is no subscript/index syntax (`s[0]`) anywhere in the Bract grammar — string indexing exists exclusively through the `at`/`sub` builtins; don't add bracket parsing as a convenience.

hints: using Python eval() to implement the bract evaluator
compiling the bract AST to Python bytecode
shortcut using exec for function calls
req-9af3.statement: (SC7) No use of Python `eval`, `exec`, or `compile` anywhere in `bract/` — the interpreter must be a genuine tree-walker over its own AST, not a translation layer onto Python's.

hints: if (0) not treated as falsy
why does if("") error in bract
truthy falsy condition semantics
non-boolean while condition
req-b6fd.statement: (Q1) The condition of `if` and `while` must evaluate to a Boolean; any other type (including 0, "", nil) is a runtime type error `line N: condition must be a boolean` — there is no truthy/falsy coercion.

hints: implementing != operator in bract
unexpected character '!' error
how to write not-equals in bract
should the parser special-case !=
req-c24c.statement: (Q4) There is no `!` token and no `!=` token in Bract — a stray `!` is a lex error (`line N: unexpected character '!'`) and `!=` never reaches the parser. Not-equals is spelled `<>`.

hints: should I create a bract/core subpackage
nested module structure for the parser
where do new interpreter modules go
req-ca3d.statement: (SC2) Single-package layout: every interpreter module lives directly under `bract/` (e.g. `bract/lexer.py`) — no nested subpackages like `bract/core/parser/`.

hints: naming convention for token types

TokenType enum naming in bract

req-d3d7.statement: DESIGN.md is frozen at seed-v1; nothing in it changes after the freeze tag is applied — corrections to the implementation arrive only as task-prompt text, never as edits to DESIGN.md itself.

hints: a < b < c parse error
chained comparison support in bract
comparisons do not chain error message
why doesn't a<b<c work
req-dab1.statement: (Q6) The `comparison` grammar rule accepts at most one comp-op — `a < b < c` is a parse error (`line N: comparisons do not chain`), not left-to-right chaining. The workaround is explicit parenthesization: `(a < b) and (b < c)`.

req-e120.statement: The README must not restate Bract's full grammar or semantics; it should point to DESIGN.md instead.

hints: at(s,0) out of range error

0-indexed vs 1-indexed string builtins
sub() range is inclusive or exclusive
req-e1be.statement: (Q5) The string builtins `at`, `len`, `sub` are 1-indexed, not 0-indexed — `at("hello", 1)` is `"h"`, and `at("hello", 0)` is out of range (not the last or first character).

hints: leaving a TODO in evaluator.py after marking the task done
stub implementation marked complete
pass placeholder left in a finished module
req-e2fa.statement: (SC12) No TODO/FIXME/pass-stub left in any module reachable from `bract/__main__.py` once a task claims to have completed the feature that module implements.

hints: formatter changes output on second run
fmt is not idempotent
does running fmt twice change the file
byte-stable formatter output requirement
req-e353.statement: `bract fmt` output must be byte-stable: formatting already-formatted output must be a no-op (fmt∘fmt = fmt).

hints: what exit code should a runtime error return
lex error exit code
bract run exit code contract
non-zero exit code for something else
req-eebd.statement: Exit codes are exactly {0, 1, 2} and only ever produced by `bract run` and the top-level CLI dispatch: 0 = success, 1 = runtime error, 2 = lex/parse error (program never started executing). No other exit code is ever returned.

test command for this project

req-f276.statement: Run the project's test suite with `python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -v`.

hints: negative number division rounding in bract
floor vs truncate division
python // gives wrong result for negative dividend
implementing bract's / operator for negative operands
req-f5d1.statement: Integer division and remainder truncate toward zero for mixed-sign operands, never floor; do not use Python's `/` or `//` directly for this since neither truncates toward zero for negative operands.
